subject: Demo: Redwood platform — calendar time ambiguous for APAC attendee

From: Emily Park <emily@atlashealth.io>

Cc: Ravi Menon <ravi@atlashealth.io>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Quick demo — timezone glitch when booking for APAC teammate

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the quick reply on the form. We're excited to see Redwood in action — can we book a 30-min demo next week? I tried your Calendly link but it shows local times that don't match my teammate in Singapore (she's in SGT / UTC+8). When I pick a slot it looks right for me (PDT) but she gets an invite two hours off.

Attached a screenshot of the Calendly picker — it looks like the dropdown defaulted to Europe for her. We typically use Chili Piper internally and sometimes run into TZ param issues when someone is logged in from a different region.

Preferable windows: 2027-04-05 afternoon PDT (evening SGT) or 2027-04-06 morning PDT. Can you confirm a time that will show correctly for both of us? Also -- does your ICS export include a time zone specification or is it just an UTC timestamp?

Thanks,
Emily Park
Program Manager, AtlasHealth
emily@atlashealth.io

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Quick demo — timezone glitch when booking for APAC teammate

Hi Emily — thanks for the details and the screenshot.

Short answer: we can absolutely avoid the Calendly/Chili Piper picker by sending a manual ICS with the TZ explicitly set, and I'll confirm the meeting in multiple zones in the body. Our Calendly link should pass a timezone query param (tz=), but some enterprise SSO/custom integrations override it which looks like what happened here.

Propose these slots (all shown below as PDT / SGT):
- Tue Apr 5 3:00pm PDT / Wed Apr 6 7:00am SGT (30m)
- Wed Apr 6 9:30am PDT / Wed Apr 6 1:30am SGT (this is borderline; prefer the first)

Can you confirm that your teammate is in Singapore (SGT, UTC+8) and that Tue Apr 5 3:00pm PDT / Wed Apr 6 7:00am SGT works? If yes I'll send a manual ICS (explicit TZ) and avoid the scheduling link. I'll cc our ops lead to track the Calendly param issue.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Thanks — confirmed: my colleague Priya is in Singapore (SGT, UTC+8). The first slot (Tue Apr 5 3:00pm PDT / Wed Apr 6 7:00am SGT) works for us.

The Chili Piper/Calendly mix is messy for us because our internal SSO sometimes forces a locale on the widget; we can continue with a manual invite. FYI I exported the ICS that Calendly sent earlier and it showed an 00:00 offset and our calendar client interpreted that as local time (resulting in a 2-hour shift). I'll attach the ICS so you can see how it looks on our end.

Looking forward to the demo.
Emily

Karthik — quick ops note: Dylan and I dug into the Calendly embed. Two actionable items:
1) For immediate scheduling, send a manual ICS with a VTIMEZONE block for Asia/Singapore (Olson TZ) and an explicit DTSTART/DTEND with TZID. That avoids client-local interpretation.
2) On engineering side, add tz param fallback: if ?tz= is present, surface it as a strong preference in the embed and include it in the invite export. We suspect the SSO/CSP is stripping the query param.

I'll log a ticket with infra (Jira: SCHED-278) and add a short snippet to our support KB with how to craft ICS payloads for customers in mixed regions. For this thread: Karthik, go ahead and send the ICS for Tue Apr 5 3:00pm PDT / Wed Apr 6 7:00am SGT. I'll attach a templated ICS we use.

—Laura
Laura Bennett

Hi Emily / Ravi — confirmed and manual invite attached. Please accept the invite and the meeting will appear as:
- 2027-04-05 15:00 PDT (Pacific Daylight Time) — Karthik (Redwood)
- 2027-04-06 07:00 SGT (Singapore Time) — Priya (AtlasHealth)

Notes:
- ICS includes VTIMEZONE:Asia/Singapore and TZID on DTSTART/DTEND to ensure clients that read TZ info will keep the correct local time. If your calendar client still shows an offset, let me know the client (Outlook web/desktop, Google Calendar mobile, Apple Calendar) and we'll send an alternate format.
- We avoided the scheduling widget to prevent SSO locale overrides; Laura has logged SCHED-278 to make the embed respect ?tz= in exports.
